scope: Browser terrain backing-store retention, projected bounds and cache ownership. Not Gold observations, native performance, total process RSS or GPU-memory qualification.

implementation.eviction: Least recently used chunks evicted before allocating another backing store. Replaced, evicted, invalidated and disposed canvases explicitly reset dimensions to zero.
implementation.viewDensity: Power-of-two density retains at least one sample per displayed device pixel when zoomed out with the supported DPR ceiling2; existing100%2x grid retained. Scale changes invalidate cache.
implementation.bounds: Exact projected vertex extrema with padding for border posts, aligned to the backing raster grid. Coarse culling is followed by actual projected bounds.
implementation.ownership: Session identity, viewing player, navigation/visibility signature, palette, assets and disposal respected.
implementation.diagnostics: Retained entries and RGBA capacity, per-frame drawn raster capacity and rebuilt chunk count. These are resource dimensions/counters, not RSS or GPU measurements.

negativeControl: Full browser regression against frozen published renderer plus read-only memory getter fails at81,920,000retainedbytes. Wider pan returns with130,744,320bytes instead ofinitial49,152,000. No original assets or browser API replacements.
rejectedFirstPolicy: Initial64MiB eviction alone caused repeated rasterization, around140ms per stress-view draw. Retained as diagnostic evidence; final minimum-zoom repeated draws rebuild zero chunks.

browser.scope: Actual Canvas renderer and public engineering sessions with an empty or authored one-pixel atlas. Capacity covers retained terrain backing stores, not total RSS or GPU memory. Frame bytes sum the raster capacity drawn; timings are host measurements, not a cross-host frame-rate qualification. No original media or Gold runtime observations.

pixelComparison.scope: Exact native100%pixel comparison against unchanged published game renderer. Authored worlds and empty atlas; not Gold runtime observations.
